_note:
Slots for [brg_team-apply]. Declared beside the fragment so a slot and its {{token}} ship in one commit. Generated into website/acf/ by `python3 kit/build-acf.py`; never hand-edit an acf.json. Defaults are the exact production copy. Slot names are underscore-only. `text`/`textarea` defaults are esc_html'd on fill, so write literal characters, never `&` or `—`. NOTE the

IS wired here, unlike careers-apply's. The rule is not 'display type is never editable' — it is that copy whose layout depends on structural markup stays as code. This heading has no
and no inline span: it is a single sentence that free-wraps inside `max-width:20ch` by design, so substituted copy wraps the same way authored copy does. `data-head="words"` is unaffected — brgw.js splits whatever text is in the DOM at runtime. The doodle cluster bleeding off the bottom-right corner is decorative and stays as code.

heading.label: Heading
heading.doc: The question, in the display face at up to 3.5rem. Wraps inside 20ch by design, so length is forgiving — but past ~60 characters it starts pushing the band taller than the comp's proportions.
heading.default: Want to be part of the team?

sub.label: Sub copy
sub.doc: One paragraph beneath the heading, capped at 60ch. Plain text; markup is escaped.
sub.default: We're always looking for people who lead with heart, stay stoked under pressure, and believe a great guest experience starts with a great team experience.

cta_label.label: Button label
cta_label.doc: Black button on the teal band. ~18 characters.

cta_href.label: Button link
cta_href.doc: Where the button goes. Defaults to the careers page.

section_bg.label: Section background
section_bg.doc: A pattern or photo filling this whole section, behind everything else. Leave it empty — as it is now — and the section keeps the plain color it has today; nothing changes until you choose something. It is cropped to fill, so the exact size does not matter. ON A DARK SECTION USE A LIGHT OR GRAY ARTWORK: a black pattern over a black panel stays invisible however high you set the strength below.

section_bg_opacity.label: Background strength
section_bg_opacity.doc: How strongly the background shows through. Choose 100% when the artwork already has the intended strength built into the file — anything lower then fades a graphic that was supplied ready to use. Use the lower values when a full-strength image would compete with the words in front of it.

section_bg_px.label: Background movement
section_bg_px.doc: Drifts the background as the page scrolls, behind the content, as a percentage of the section's height. 0 is off — the right starting point, because a pattern moving too fast pulls the eye away from the copy. 6 is subtle, 10 medium, 16 strong, and anything in between is allowed. 40 is the ceiling; the page stops there.

section_bg_px_dir.label: Background movement direction
section_bg_px_dir.doc: Which way the background travels as the page scrolls. Only matters once movement above is above 0. Neighboring sections set in opposite directions are what reads as depth rather than as one sheet sliding.

section_bg_mobile.label: Section background — phones
section_bg_mobile.doc: Optional. A version of the background for phones, used below 768px wide. Leave it empty and the main background above is used at every size. Worth setting when the main artwork is wide: cropped to a narrow screen it often shows nothing recognizable, and a tall or simplified version reads far better.

mark_1_all_trim_art.label: Artwork
mark_1_all_trim_art.doc: Which mark is drawn here. Leave it alone to keep the one the design uses. Any SVG or PNG from the media library works; SVG stays crisp at any size.

mark_1_all_trim_pos.label: Position
mark_1_all_trim_pos.doc: Where the mark sits in its section. "Where the design put it" is the starting point and leaves it exactly where it is now — choose one of the nine only when you want to move it. Corners sit inside the section padding, so a long headline cannot push a mark down into the type.

mark_1_all_trim_opacity.label: Opacity
mark_1_all_trim_opacity.doc: How solid the mark is. 100 is as drawn; lower settles it into the background.

mark_1_all_trim_show.label: Show this mark
mark_1_all_trim_show.doc: Hiding removes just this one mark. Nothing else in the section changes.

mark_1_all_trim_anim.label: Animation
mark_1_all_trim_anim.doc: How the mark moves. "As built" keeps what it does today — a hard-cut jitter for most, a spin for the asterisk in the hero cluster. Still stops it entirely. Anyone who has switched off animation in their system settings sees it still whatever is chosen here.
